national.title: Armed man arrested near White House planned to kill Trump, DHS says
national.summary: Secret Service officers found three weapons in the vehicle of the suspect, who allegedly told officers he had heard voices in his head telling him to come to Washington and assassinate the president.
national.body: An undocumented immigrant armed with several weapons was taken into custody within blocks of the White House Thursday night after he allegedly told Secret Service officers that he was planning an attempt on President Trump's life, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security said.The suspect, identified as Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos of Venezuela, was arrested on three counts each of unlawful transportation of a firearm, carrying unregistered firearms and carrying unregistered ammunition, along with one count each of possession of certain dangerous weapons, carrying a pistol without a license, unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, theft and receiving stolen property, DHS said in a news release Friday. Secret Service officers observed the suspect acting suspiciously in his vehicle and approached him while he was parked on Constitution Avenue, DHS said. A law enforcement source told CBS News the incident took place in the 1600 block of Constitution Avenue NW, near the Ellipse.When officers confronted the suspect, DHS said, he allegedly told them that he had heard voices in his head telling him to come to Washington, D.C., and assassinate Mr. Trump. The Secret Service officers learned the suspect's vehicle had been reported stolen, DHS said, and the suspect allegedly admitted there were weapons in the vehicle. When officers searched the vehicle, they found three firearms, including a rifle, as well as dozens of rounds of ammunition, according to DHS, which released a photo of the seized items. "This is the latest example of Secret Service personnel relying on extensive training and experience to deescalate a volatile situation that posed an imminent threat to our protectees and other Americans," Secret Service Director Sean Curran said in a statement.DHS said the suspect entered the U.S. through Texas in March 2024 and was arrested by U.S. Border Patrol, but was later released. It was not immediately clear if he had an attorney. "Thanks to our brave Secret Service officers, this illegal alien with three firearms in his vehicle was arrested near the White House before he could harm anyone," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a separate statement.Mr. Trump has been the target of multiple assassination attempts since entering political life, most notably a shooting at a rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, during his second presidential campaign in July 2

national.summary: President Trump announced that Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff just hours after he told 60 Minutes that he'd be shaking up his team.
national.body: President Trump announced that Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff just hours after he told 60 Minutes that he'd be shaking up his team.When 60 Minutes Correspondent Ross Douthat asked Mr. Trump whether he expected to fire anyone after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress, the president said: "I do, yeah. Little bit.""I love my Cabinet. I think they're good," he said. "But I'll … be doing maybe a few changes."Mr. Trump suggested Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is safe for now, despite CBS News reporting that he asked advisers this week whether the Pentagon chief should stick around. When Douthat asked whether he has confidence in Hegseth, Mr. Trump said: "I do.""Look, we've won two wars. We've won Venezuela and taken out billions and billions and billions of dollars already. And we will be taking out many billions of dollars and get along very well. And, you could call it a territory, you could call it whatever you want. We won that war in less than one hour," Mr. Trump said.After announcing Wiles' departure on Friday, Mr. Trump told reporters he "wanted to make a change," adding, "sometimes in life, you have to make moves." Wiles submitted her resignation on Thursday, a move that was tied to the GOP's midterm defeats, CBS News reported.Wiles is among the most powerful people to leave the Trump administration. A few Cabinet officials departed earlier this year — Attorney General Pam Bondi, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer — but otherwise, the president who rose to nationwide fame by firing people on television has largely left his team intact.Watch the interview on 60 Minutes on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 7 p.m. ET/PT on CBS and Paramount+. national.summary: Democrats won sizable House and Senate majorities in the 2026 midterm elections, but the exact margins are unclear because some races haven't been projected yet. Here's where the results stand.
national.body: Washington — The makeup of Congress shifted dramatically in the 2026 midterm elections, as Democrats decisively won control of the Senate and picked up dozens of House seats — in what's on track to be one of the largest midterm routs in recent decades.The exact margins of Congress are not yet clear, as winners have not yet been projected in two Senate races and more than two dozen House races. They include GOP-held districts with razor-thin margins, a few Democratic seats that could flip to Republicans and several races in California and other Western states that still need to count ballots.Here's a look at the congressional races that CBS News has not yet projected, including where the results stand:Senate Toss-UpsDemocrats are set to enter next year with at least 54 Senate seats, compared to Republicans' 44. Two Senate races still haven't been called — one has long been viewed as a battleground, and the other came out of nowhere.Alaska Senate: Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan is running for reelection against Democrat Mary Peltola, a razor-thin race rocked by a last-minute scandal over how another Dan Sullivan got on the ballot. The count could drag on due to both outstanding ballots and Alaska's ranked choice voting system, which allows voters to rank candidates in order of preference. If no candidate is the top choice of a majority of voters, the last-place candidate is eliminated and the counting process moves to a second round. Final results aren't expected until 15 days after Election Day. Both the Sullivan and Peltola campaigns have argued they have the upper hand.Mississippi Senate: The race between GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom was not widely expected to be competitive, but it remains a toss-up. national.title: Cornell faculty pass no-confidence vote over leadership's handling of Jane Doe allegations
national.summary: Friday's resolution by academic staff is largely symbolic as they do not have the power to remove those in charge of the university.
national.body:
Cornell University's academic staff have passed a vote of no confidence over its leadership's handling of what staff call a "crisis of sexual assault" after a former student alleged she was gang raped while attending.

The woman, known anonymously as Jane Doe, is suing her former university and the fraternity over an alleged incident involving several men at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024.

All seven of the accused have denied wrongdoing when contacted by the BBC's US partner CBS. None has been charged with a crime.

Friday's no-confidence vote passed by 75 votes to 50. It is largely symbolic because the faculty senate does not have the power to remove leaders.

The resolution states that the faculty senate, which represents academic staff, "has no confidence in the ability of the central administration to effectively address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault at Cornell University".

It did not make any specific recommendations or suggest what administrators did wrong in response to the accusation.

It is a rebuke of university leaders including President Michael Kotlikoff, whom Doe has accused of asking why she waited several weeks to report the incident.

The Ivy League institution in upstate New York has said her account of Kotlikoff's reaction is "incorrect".

national.body: Washington â The White House's page listing financial disclosure forms for President Trump and top White House officials went offline without explanation Friday afternoon, only to be restored after CBS News inquired about its removal. The page, whitehouse.gov/disclosures, serves as a hub for various disclosures required by law, including the president's annual financial disclosure form and periodic stock transaction reports. It includes financial records for the president, vice president and more than 100 White House staffers, including Susie Wiles and Stephen Miller. CBS News uses an automated system to monitor ethics disclosures across the government, including those posted on the White House page. The system checks for new filings every 30 minutes. The White House hub was still operational as of 3:01 p.m. Friday, but returned a 404 error at the next routine check at 3:31 p.m., indicating it had been taken down. The disclosure documents themselves were still online.At 4:20 p.m., CBS News asked the White House press office in an email whether the page had been intentionally removed or whether it was down due to a technical error. CBS News requested a response by 5 p.m. The White House did not reply.As CBS News prepared a story on the page's removal, the automated ethics monitor flagged that it was back online, having been restored sometime between 4:31 and 5:01 p.m. The publish time in the source code of the White House page was 22:00:00+00:00, or 5:00:00 p.m. ET.The White House did not respond to a request for clarification about why the page went down or why it was restored.When the page came back online, there was one new file listed: a report on the president's stock trades that he signed on Sept. 17. Data from the White House server show it was uploaded at 3:14 p.m. The White House has previously posted stock reports within a few days from when they were posted on OGE's site.The financial disclosures listed on the page are required to be filed under the Ethics in Government Act of 1978, and the periodic stock reports under the 2012 STOCK Act. national.title: With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle
national.summary: The US president's promotion of Miller, a loyal partisan firebrand to be his new chief of staff sets up likely clashes with Congress.
national.body:
North America correspondent Published 1 hour ago In the aftermath of the Republican Party's sweeping defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections, Donald Trump said he would be willing to work with the newly ascendent Democrats in Congress.

On Friday, however, he elevated Stephen Miller, his bare-knuckled political operative and longtime adviser, to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.

Far from an olive branch to Congress, Miller's promotion could be a sign that the president is girding for political battle by installing a partisan firebrand in the top White House job.

"The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our president and defend this magnificent republic," Miller posted on X, adding that he was "honored beyond words" to be Trump's pick for the job.

One of the most powerful positions in Washington, the chief of staff is gatekeeper to the president, agenda-setter in the White House and chief negotiator with Congress and other outside political interests.

"Stephen Miller's been with me since the beginning," Trump said in comments to reporters after announcing the move on his Truth Social website. "He gets it."

Miller is best known for being the driving force behind the Trump administration's aggressive immigration enforcement policies, which has included ramping up funding for enforcement operations across the US.

He made headlines when he called Alex Pretti, who was shot and killed by federal immigration officials during a massive deportation operation in Minneapolis, a "domestic terrorist" and an "assassin". He would later walk back those words, saying federal agents "may not have been following" proper protocol.

national.title: Democrats win Senate control — live updates
national.summary: Democrats were able to pick up the seats needed to gain control of the Senate, CBS News projects, and the party scored several upset victories in red states.
national.body: The U.S. Senate race in Mississippi remains a toss-up between incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom. As of Friday evening, Colom was leading by about 2,500 votes. According to Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson , there are approximately 3,600 outstanding mail ballots and an unknown number of affidavit ballots, or provisional ballots, from voters whose eligibility needs to be confirmed. Absentee ballots must be received within five business days, while affidavit ballots must be processed within the 10-day window that counties have to certify results, which ends Nov 13. Both parties are keeping a close eye on the process. CBS News has confirmed the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee has deployed lawyers and resources to the state to monitor the count. "I'm confident that ultimately Mississippi has decided to go in a new direction," Colum told reporters after greeting campaign volunteers Thursday morning in Jackson. The National Republican Senatorial Committee and Hyde-Smith campaign filed a request for all counties to separate and preserve all affidavit ballots. The Colom campaign called the move a "desperate stunt." His counsel also sent a new letter to Mississippi's 82 counties asking them to respect election procedures. Hyde-Smith predicted that she will represent Mississippi for another six-year term, posting on X : "We believe thousands of votes remain to be counted from dozens of Republican counties, and we are confident those votes will reinforce her path to victory." At a news conference Thursday, Mississippi Republican Party Chair Mike Hurst insisted the election "is far from being over" and noted the state party has attorneys and observers throughout the state to ensure all legally cast ballots are counted. Mississippi does not allow recounts, so a winner will be decided based on a plurality of votes.

national.title: Cornell's Faculty Senate votes "no confidence" in administration
national.summary: Cornell University's Faculty Senate approved a resolution expressing no confidence in the university's administration, including Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff and other administrators.
national.body: Cornell University's Faculty Senate approved a resolution expressing no confidence in the university's administration, including Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff and other administrators. It's a major rebuke of the university's leadership. Members of the faculty told CBS News New York the resolution questioned whether Cornell's administration can effectively address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault on campus. The vote, which passed 75-50, is largely symbolic and does not require university leadership to step down. Five faculty senators abstained and five others did not vote. "We distanced ourselves from this leadership and said they don't speak for us. They are not the Cornell we know and love," resolution co-sponsor and faculty senator Iris Packman said. "Our vision for Cornell is one of zero tolerance for sexual assault." The vote follows weeks of outrage over Cornell's handling of sexual assault allegations, including Jane Doe's 2024 alleged gang rape case. All seven men accused of wrongdoing in her lawsuit deny the allegations. "We created this resolution after hearing from scores of current students, alumni, staff and faculty that the Jane Doe case was the tip of an iceberg," resolution sponsor Paul Ortiz said. "This vote is a reckoning for our University. It is a call for real, systemic change; not a slow-moving taskforce, weakly enforced ban on fraternity parties, or expensive PR damage control, but meaningful, evidence-based steps to reduce the incidence of sexual assault on campus and provide significant support to and justice for survivors," sponsors of the measure said in a statement. "We believe that the Faculty Senate did not reach this decision lightly and considered all available information," Doe's attorney Thomas Giuffra said in a statement. "We are hopeful that this will be yet another step forward to educate the Cornell community by addressing the longstanding scourge of sexual assault on campus." national.body:
The Democrats hold a narrow lead over the Republicans in the US Senate race in Mississippi, with both sides in a dispute over the counting of the remaining votes which could decide the outcome.

Lawyers for each campaign are preparing for a possible legal battle over the final results and weighing in on the examination of ballots.

The result could mark the end of almost 40 years of Republican control over Mississippi's senate seats and will determine the size of the Democrats' majority in the upper house.

Mississippi is the only US state which does not have a set procedure in place to trigger a recount - and the pressure is on to declare a winner with the state's 13 November deadline for certification approaching.

With 97% of the votes counted as of Friday, Democratic candidate Scott Colom is about 2,500 votes ahead of the incumbent Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith.

Mississippi's Secretary of State Michael Watson said on Wednesday that 3,600 "absentee-by-mail ballots" were still to be counted. The state can accept these votes so long as they were postmarked by election day and are received by 10 November.

Watson said there are also an "unknown" number of provisional ballots, also known as affidavit ballots, to be counted. These are typically cast when a voter lacked the required identification to cast their vote. The deadline for voters to resolve any ID issues with provisional ballots, usually by providing acceptable photo identification, is also 10 November.

Mississippi Republican Party Chair Michael Hurst said on Thursday that they estimated there could be "approximately 20,000 outstanding ballots left to be counted".

national.summary: Archaeologists who led a dig at a monumental tomb in Siberia said they turned up evidence of the earliest known use of cannabis for psychoactive purposes.
national.body:
Jamey Keaten, Associated Press Jamey Keaten, Associated Press

Philipp Jenne, Associated Press Philipp Jenne, Associated Press

GENEVA (AP) — People may have been getting high off cannabis earlier than previously thought — at least 2,800 years ago, a new study suggests.

Archaeologists who led a dig at a monumental tomb in Siberia said they turned up evidence of the earliest known use of cannabis for psychoactive purposes.

The findings point to cannabis consumption at least 300 years earlier than previously known use in neighboring China.

Ancient drug use has long intrigued scholars. The Greek historian Herodotus wrote about inhabitants of Central Asia smoking cannabis around 440 B.C., and recent archaeologists have found the seeds in tombs across its highlands.

The team from Germany, Russia, Sweden and Switzerland said analysis of hair in the royal tomb where cannabis seeds turned up sheds new light on the plant's role in ancient societies.

"It's extremely rare that we have both preserved plant parts and human soft tissue with the active compounds in it in the same context," said co-author Gino Caspari, an archaeologist at the University of Bern.

national.title: Dad of 20-year-old co-pilot in Florida jet crash says her final radio calls showed 'she's tough'
national.summary: "I wanted to be by her side," Allan Filgueiras, a pilot who helped teach his daughter to fly, said at a news conference Friday, at times holding back tears. "Inside the plane. To help."
national.body:
The father of the 20-year-old co-pilot who died along with eight others when their Learjet crashed in Florida said Friday he has listened to his daughter's heartbreaking final radio transmissions "many times" since the crash.

Allan Filgueiras, a pilot who helped teach his daughter to fly, was searching for answers as to why the plane plunged from the sky on Sunday. Instead, he found immense pride in how his daughter, Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, handled the crisis.

"I did listen to that many times trying to find a clue. In my head. How'd that happen? And wow, she's tough," Allan Filgueiras said at a news conference Friday.

"I wanted to be by her side," he said, at times holding back tears. "Inside the plane. To help."

In her conversation with air traffic control, Nathalia Filgueiras can first be heard calmly reporting ice buildup on the plane as it flew into a thunderstorm and turbulence tossed it up and down by 700 feet (200 meters). The situation quickly escalated as the aircraft fell at breathtaking speed. "Declare an emergency 722-Bravo-Delta. We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute!" she said.

Her father and aviation safety experts are impressed that Filgueiras continued to call out updates on what was happening even as she realized the plane's fate was sealed.

"For the family — it's like having the heart torn from my chest," her father said in Spanish. "I have to find a way to go on living."

The family wants to push back against online criticism over whether she had enough experience to be in the cockpit of a high-performance business jet. She had more than 1,300 hours of experience and completed extensive training to earn her commercial pilot's license and get certified for a Learjet. The plane's captain, 55-year-old Jeff Gregory, is believed to have been at the controls in the aircraft's final minutes.

national.title: Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck
national.summary: Musk said it was to make room for production of its Cybercabs - autonomous taxis without a driver.
national.body:
Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk says.

He did not spell out whether it plans to stop making them entirely or shift production elsewhere, but did say the decision was to "make room" for building more of its self-driving Cybercab cars.

But the project's lead engineer, Wes Morrill, appeared to suggest the vehicle was being discontinued, writing on X: "Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab."

With its distinctive angular looks, the Cybertruck attracted diehard fans, but was beset by delays before being launched in 2023 and has had disappointing sales numbers since.

Tesla fans have been mourning the news online, with one person calling it " the best vehicle Tesla has ever made , external " as he lamented it being "discontinued next year".

Musk responded to the user , external with the word "true", adding: "But the Cybertruck fleet will be around for a long time."

The vehicle has always been a passion project for Musk. He said it was " way more awesome than people realise , external " in March, and called it the " best product Tesla has ever made to date , external " in April.

But there have always been big questions about whether consumers shared that view and whether the Cybertruck could cut through and earn a spot in the US' lucrative truck market.

national.title: Cornell faculty vote 'no confidence' in university leadership after alleged fraternity gang rape
national.summary: While the faculty body has no power over the university's top leaders, backers of the resolution had said they hoped it would pressure Cornell's trustees to address longstanding institutional failures they identified.
national.body:
Leah Willingham, Associated Press Leah Willingham, Associated Press

Cornell University's Faculty Senate approved a resolution Friday declaring "no confidence" in the school's top leaders, a symbolic gesture reflecting deep discontent on campus in the wake of a former student's lawsuit saying she was gang raped at a fraternity party in 2024.

The resolution passed 75-50, with five faculty senators abstaining and five others not voting, according to an email sent to Faculty Senate members on Friday afternoon.

The vote followed weeks of debate among professors over whether Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff and other administrators handled the woman's allegations properly and have done enough to curtail sexual misconduct at the prestigious university.

While the faculty body has no power over the university's top leaders, backers of the resolution had said they hoped it would pressure Cornell's trustees to address longstanding institutional failures they identified.

Board of Trustees Chair Anne Smalling said in a statement the faculty vote "reflects the deep anger across our campus" and sent a clear signal that what happened to the woman was unacceptable, but added that Kotlikoff and his administration were the right leaders to "thoughtfully and comprehensively" address the issue.

Thomas Giuffra, an attorney for the woman who filed the lawsuit, said in a statement Friday that "we are hopeful that this will be yet another step forward to educate and support the Cornell community by addressing the longstanding scourge of sexual assault on campus."

The Cornell community has been distressed since mid-September, when a former student, identified only by the pseudonym Jane Doe in court documents, filed a lawsuit against the university and seven former members of the Chi Phi fraternity, saying she was given ketamine and raped at a fraternity house in October 2024.

Markle was arrested on a federal complaint alleging he held images that show child sex abuse, the US Department of Justice (DoJ) said.

The 82-year-old was arrested in Florida after the FBI searched two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for almost 20 years.

He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, the US Department of Justice (DoJ) said. Markle has previously denied allegations of possessing images of child sex abuse, calling them "sick lies".

Markle's court hearing lasted for 30 minutes, and the charges were laid out against him by federal prosecutor Courtenay Derry, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.

He was brought into court a wheelchair, escorted by two US Marshals. Markle was wearing black trousers and a black t-shirt.

The court ordered Markle to submit to home detention at his assisted living facility in Florida and electronic monitoring.

No plea was taken during the hearing, and an arraignment date in California will be determined in due course, a joint statement from the DoJ and the US Attorney's Office Central California said.

national.title: Democrats win the Arizona House, Senate and governor's office for the first time since 1966
national.summary: The Associated Press called enough legislative races to confirm that both chambers flipped on Friday.
national.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — Democrats in Arizona won control of both state legislative chambers and retained the governor's office, giving the party its first trifecta in the state since 1966 as Democrats made major gains nationwide in this week's elections and took control of both chambers of Congress.

In her first term, Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs had vetoed more than 540 measures passed by the Republican-led Legislature on policies including taxes, immigration and voting laws. Hobbs has said she's looking to address water issues and affordability, and take on fraud and abuse in the state's school voucher program.

The Associated Press called enough legislative races to confirm that both chambers flipped on Friday. The news organization calls races individually and it can take several days after voting, depending on when election officials tally the votes and how close the elections are. There have not been major disputes or disruptions this year.

In Arizona, Republicans have held the House for 60 years and the Senate since the early 1990s.

Overall, Democrats took full control — both statehouse chambers and governors' offices — in at least six states where they previously shared power with Republicans. Besides Arizona, those wins were in the battleground states of Michigan, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Nevada and Wisconsin.

The flips weren't just in states that are normally competitive. Democrats won control of the Texas House, which Republicans have held since 2003, and elected Gina Hinojosa as the state's first Democratic governor since George W. Bush ousted Ann Richards in 1994. Republicans held onto the state Senate.

Democrats also flipped the lower chambers of the legislatures in Maine and North Carolina and both chambers in New Hampshire, where Republican Kelly Ayotte was reelected. The count could grow as results are tallied in additional states.

The National Council of State Legislatures says it's likely to end up as the election with the most legislative seats and chambers changing parties since the 2010 election, when Republicans took over governments across the country amid the Great Recession.

Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development.

On Thursday, businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development took a hammering on stock markets, particularly chip and semiconductor makers.

But the Nasdaq Composite bounced back slightly on Friday, ending the day up 1.1%, partly reversing some of its 5.5% fall.

Companies that lost hundreds of billions in market value recovered some ground on Friday, including Nvidia, SpaceX and Tesla.

national.title: WATCH: 'Elections matter.' Houston mayor limits police cooperation with ICE
national.summary: The shift in the nation's fourth-largest city is one of the first actions to restrict U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations since Democrats' rout in Tuesday's midterm elections.
national.body:
Lekan Oyekanmi, Associated Press Lekan Oyekanmi, Associated Press

Anna Wilder, Associated Press/Report For America Anna Wilder, Associated Press/Report For America

Valerie Gonzalez, Associated Press Valerie Gonzalez, Associated Press

HOUSTON (AP) — Houston's mayor on Friday directed police to limit cooperation with federal immigration authorities, signing an order that he called a direct result of Democrats reclaiming power in Texas for the first time in decades.

The shift in the nation's fourth-largest city is one of the first actions to restrict U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations since Democrats' rout in Tuesday's midterm elections. It also is a sign that results are already having an impact in Texas, where Republican leaders have enthusiastically embraced President Donald Trump's mass deportation agenda.

The stunning victories included Democrat Gina Hinojosa ousting Republican Gov. Greg Abbott , which will make her Texas' first Latina governor and the first member of her party to hold the office in more than 30 years.

"I've said many times, elections matter," Mayor John Whitmire said.

Whitmire, a Democrat, said the city would go after immigrants "that pose a danger, not those that are going about their family business, work and education." In the case of a traffic incident, "you write a citation or you warn them and they go about their way," he said.

national.title: Trump's triumphal arch is blocked for now, but a new website highlights the plans
national.summary: The White House highlighted the website the morning after U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan issued a temporary restraining order that prohibits work on the site for 14 days.
national.body:
Will Weissert, Associated Press Will Weissert, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — A federal court has temporarily blocked President Donald Trump from breaking ground for his towering memorial arch, but that hasn't stopped his administration from pushing forward with the plans for building it, starting with a glitzy new website launched Friday.

The site's debut is yet another sign of how much Trump is leaning into his efforts to make over the White House and Washington to his own gilded tastes, even after his party lost control of Congress in a midterm-election drubbing. It was the fourth day this week alone that the administration promoted his projects.

The website declares that the 250-foot (76-meter) structure — which is slated to rise in a mass of blindingly gold ornamentation and stately gray granite between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery — will be formally known as the United States Military Triumphal Arch.

Describing the arch as "an American vision finally realized," the site offers bird's-eye views of the proposal from many angles and shows off the declarations it will feature: "One Nation Under God" on one side and "Golden Age of America" on another. It's also set to have towering gold doors complete with panels of sculptures at its base.

At its very top, the structure features a golden-hued cherub hoisting a flaming torch that recalls a smaller version of the Statue of Liberty.

The website does not say how much the project will cost or how it will be paid for, although some estimates have reached as high as $100 million.

The White House highlighted the website the morning after U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan issued a temporary restraining order that prohibits work on the site for 14 days. That order followed a vote to approve the arch by a federal planning commission that is stocked with Trump's allies.

national.body:
President Donald Trump has named Stephen Miller, the architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new chief of staff following historic losses in the US midterm elections.

Miller replaces Susie Wiles, who submitted her resignation after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress, delivering a blow to the prospects for Trump's agenda in his final two years in the White House.

Speaking to reporters, Trump said Wiles had "done a very good job", but "we've got to make moves sometimes".

Miller, a Trump loyalist and deputy chief of staff who served as a senior adviser during his first administration, is set to take on the new role on Monday.

One of Trump's closest aides, Miller, 41, stuck by the president following his 2020 election defeat and followed Trump back into power last year.

On X, Miller called Trump "the most transformative political leader in American History" who has "single-handedly saved America from those who would destroy it".

He thanked Wiles for her years of devoted service to the president, country and for her friendship.

"The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our President and defend this magnificent Republic," he wrote.

national.title: Trump's global health strategy is emerging. What will the Democratic Congress say?
national.summary: The Trump Administration has ushered in a fundamental shift in the U.S. approach to global health aid. How will the newly elected Democratic Congress weigh in?
national.body:
At an October meeting, signed copies of the health cooperation memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Zambia are displayed by U.S. Embassy Chargé d'Affaires Mich Coker (left) and Zambia's Minister of Finance and National Planning Situmbeko Musokotwane (center). Minister of Health Roma Chilengi (right) applauds. U.S Embassy in Zambia hide caption

By all appearances, it was a classic government ceremony. Officials in suits. Big black chairs around a wooden table. A cluster of microphones. It happened on October 8 in Lusaka, Zambia. Amid applause, U.S. and Zambian officials signed a global health agreement, called a Memorandum of Understanding or MOU.

But Mich Coker — the Chargé d'Affaires at the U.S. Embassy in Zambia — said this agreement was anything but classic.

"This MOU represents a fundamental shift," he said, speaking at the signing ceremony . He explained that the relationship between the two countries was moving "from a traditional donor-recipient model to a true partnership, one grounded in Zambian leadership, in Zambian ownership and in shared accountability."

Global health experts on all sides of the political spectrum and all over the world agree with Coker that there's been a fundamental shift in the U.S. approach to global health.

"The shift that's currently unfolding is very large and it's very rapid," says Janeen Madan Keller, acting co-director of the Global Health Program at the Center for Global Development.

The story of this fundamental shift starts at the beginning of the second Trump Administration with months of global health turmoil — Madan Keller and other experts say — but has given way to a clearer strategy. One with big goals, a short timeline and a lot less transparency than what came before.

Here is a look at where things stand now and how a Congress controlled by the Democratic Party might impact the new landscape.

national.title: Connecticut Sen. Chris Murphy released from hospital after stroke
national.summary: The 53-year-old Democrat said in a statement Friday that doctors are "encouraged by the progress" he's made so far.
national.body:
Kevin Freking, Associated Press Kevin Freking, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — Connecticut Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy says he has been discharged from the hospital after suffering a stroke last weekend and will miss "several weeks" of votes in the Senate as he recovers in a rehabilitation facility.

Murphy, 53, said in a statement Friday that doctors are "encouraged by the progress" he's made so far.

Murphy says doctors diagnosed him with a small hemorrhagic stroke, which is a bleed in the brain. Murphy says he called 911 last Saturday after feeling that "something was not right" with his body.

"This has been a scary experience for me and my family, and I appreciate the continued respect for our privacy," he said.

In the Senate, Murphy serves on the Appropriations Committee and is a leading voice on immigration and gun policy. He is considered a contender for more senior leadership positions in the Senate and among the many Democrats seen as potential 2028 candidates for the White House.

Three other Senate Democrats have had strokes in recent years.

Sens. Ben Ray Lujan of New Mexico and Chris Van Hollen of Maryland had strokes in 2022 and have since recovered. Pennsylvania Sen. John Fetterman had a stroke while campaigning for his seat that same year and now uses adaptive technology in the Senate, including live captioning on a phone or tablet that transcribes words as people speak to him and helps him process the conversation.

local.title: State hails completion of Route 5 bridge project
local.summary: Work on a town of Dunkirk bridge has been officially completed. New York state Department of Transportation Commissioner Marie Therese Dominguez Friday said the $3.4 million project on State Route 5 replaced the nearly 100-year-old bridge over Canadaway Creek with a modern structure that will enhanc
local.body:
Work on a town of Dunkirk bridge has been officially completed.

New York state Department of Transportation Commissioner Marie Therese Dominguez Friday said the $3.4 million project on State Route 5 replaced the nearly 100-year-old bridge over Canadaway Creek with a modern structure that will enhance safety and ease travel for motorists, cyclists and pedestrians along this important road in Western New York. This stretch of State Route 5 is part of the historic Great Lakes Seaway Trail and is a popular route for sightseers as well as local commuters and commercial vehicles traveling through the scenic Lake Erie corridor.

"State Route 5 is an integral part of everyday life for the people who live along this stretch of Chautauqua County as well as the many visitors who come to take in the area's natural beauty and charm," Commissioner Dominguez said. "Thanks to Governor Hochul's commitment to making smart investments in our infrastructure and public safety, this project delivered a bridge that's built to last while also making the route more accessible for bicyclists and pedestrians."

The project included construction of a new 115-foot-long by 43-foot-wide bridge with one lane of traffic in each direction and new eight-foot shoulders to better accommodate bicyclists and pedestrians. Work also included stabilization of the banks of Canadaway Creek to help minimize erosion. The adjacent Canadaway Creek Nature Sanctuary was not impacted by the project.

“It is with great relief that this well-traveled bridge along the Seaway Trail reached its completion before the deadline that was given to us,” Dunkirk Town Supervisor Shari Miller said. “The Chautauqua County NYSDOT team was great to work with and very responsive to our concerns. When we needed more signage, they responded immediately. I am very happy to have traffic flowing again.”

The new bridge also features an enhanced steel protection system designed to prevent corrosion and extend the structure's service life. The process included spraying molten metal onto the steel girders, combined with a new specialized paint technology to provide added protection against the elements and improve the bridge's long-term durability.

Chautauqua County Executive PJ Wendel said, "This $3.4 million investment is a win for Chautauqua County and everyone who relies on Route 5. The new Canadaway Creek bridge improves safety and strengthens a vital connection for our residents, businesses, and visitors traveling along the beautiful Lake Erie shoreline. I want to thank the New York State Department of Transportation for making this project a reality. Investments like these are essential to keeping our communities connected and our region moving forward."

local.summary: The village of Fredonia, in coordination with the Chautauqua County Health Department, has lifted the conserve water order for all Village of Fredonia water customers, including customers in the Town of Pomfret. The conserve water order was issued on Friday, Oct. 23 to reduce demand on Fredonia’s wa
local.body:
The village of Fredonia, in coordination with the Chautauqua County Health Department, has lifted the conserve water order for all Village of Fredonia water customers, including customers in the Town of Pomfret.

The conserve water order was issued on Friday, Oct. 23 to reduce demand on Fredonia’s water treatment plant. However, water usage did not decrease significantly following the order, and the plant continues to experience challenges due to high levels of organic material in the Fredonia Reservoir and the old media in the filter beds.

The water treatment plant has consistently produced water that meets New York State Department of Health drinking water safety standards in recent days. To maintain safe drinking water, the plant must maintain a steady filter backwashing schedule, which requires a significant volume of the treated water that is produced at the water treatment plant.

Because water conservation efforts did not result in a significant reduction in customer demand, additional steps were taken to help relieve pressure on the treatment plant. On November 6, Town of Pomfret water customers located south and east of the Routes 60 and 20 intersection were transitioned from the Fredonia water system to the North Chautauqua County Water District. This transition had already been planned for 2027 and the Town of Pomfret did provide Fredonia with appropriate notice prior to the recent conserve and boil water orders. By making this switch now, rather than later, the municipalities aim to reduce stress on Fredonia's water treatment plant.

These measures will help the Village of Fredonia continue providing safe drinking water while addressing ongoing challenges at its water treatment plant.

entertainment.title: ‘Ellen DeGeneres Show’ producer Matt Wright’s cause of death revealed
entertainment.summary: Page Six previously reported exclusively that Wright had been suffering from "heart problems" prior to his passing.
entertainment.body:
Ellen DeGeneres’ producer Matthew Wright’s cause of death has been revealed after his sudden death at the age of 52.

The producer — who worked on “The Ellen DeGeneres Show” for 16 years — died from cardiopulmonary arrest on Oct. 30, per a death certificate obtained by People .

Hypertension was listed as an underlying cause, with obstructive sleep apnea and Class II obesity noted as contributing factors to his death, per the outlet.

Page Six previously reported exclusively that Wright had been suffering from “heart problems” prior to his passing.

DeGeneres, 68, reflected on Wright’s death in an Instagram tribute posted Nov. 2.

“God, he was an amazing guy,” she shared. “He made me laugh; he would surprise me with things he did all the time.”

“He was smart, he was kind … I mean, everyone loved him,” she continued. “I loved him. And it’s just shocking, it’s shocking.”

Wright passed in “an unfathomable tragedy” while working remotely in Los Angeles, according to a GoFundMe set up to help his husband, Justin, and his family pay for funeral costs.

entertainment.title: Michael Sanft, Attorney Who Represented Keffe D in 2Pac Murder Trial, Dies at 54
entertainment.summary: Sanft put together a team and took on Davis' case pro bono.
entertainment.body:
Michael Sanft, the defense attorney who represented Duane “Keffe D” Davis during the 2Pac murder trial , has died, FOX5 Las Vegas reported. He was 54 years old.

Sanft put together a team and took on Davis’ case pro bono while serving as the lead trial attorney for the Vegas-based SOS Injury Lawyers, where he has tried more than 150 cases. After the highly publicized trial, he told FOX5 Las Vegas that he didn’t have any regrets. Related Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania Weezer to Receive Legend of Live Award at 2026 Billboard Live Music Summit Explore 2Pac Tupac Shakur See latest videos, charts and news

“Maybe if I had a psychic sitting next to me to help discern who should be on the jury,” he told the outlet. “We had the best team possible in this case, from the motion practice work on this appeal to our investigator to our firm here at SOS Injury. We all did our part. I don’t see what I could’ve done differently.”

Thirty years after the 25-year-old Tupac Shakur was killed in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas following a Mike Tyson fight, the now-63-year-old Keffe D was found guilty for his role in orchestrating the killing and sentenced to 40 years in prison. “You don’t get to take a man from his family, you don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur,” Judge Carli Kierny told Davis as she handed down his sentencing. “It took us 30 years, but at this time you are going to face justice for what you did on Sept. 7, 1996.”

Sanft reportedly died on Thursday night in Las Vegas. No cause of death has been confirmed as the details surrounding his passing have been limited so far.

entertainment.title: Grey's Anatomy Actor Harry Shum Jr. Starred In A Fantasy Drama Based On A Popular Book Series
entertainment.summary: Before he joined the staff of Grey Sloan Memorial Hospital as Dr. Benson Kwan, Harry Shum Jr. played one of the best characters in this YA TV series.
entertainment.body:
"Shadowhunters" was based on "The Mortal Instruments" YA book series by Cassandra Clare. The fantasy show is about human-angel hybrids who have special abilities and hunt demons. Shum's Magnus has centuries' worth of experience with magic and uses his prowess to help the main character, Clary Fray (Katherine McNamara), and other Shadowhunters. Magnus is also bisexual, and his relationship with Alec Lightwood (Matthew Daddario) is popular within the fandom and the LGBTQ+ community.

Freeform/YouTube Spanning three seasons, "Shadowhunters" is the most successful live-action adaptation of Clare's six-book "Mortal Instruments" series, but it isn't the only one. Before the fantasy show aired on Freeform, there was a 2013 film adaptation titled "The Mortal Instruments: City of Bones" — based on the first novel. Shum, who's currently competing on "Dancing with the Stars," auditioned for the movie, but wouldn't become a part of the supernatural universe until the TV show premiered.

In the movie, Magnus is played by Godfrey Gao. A sequel was planned but never materialized. Although Shum didn't land a role in the movie version of "The Mortal Instruments," he already had an advantage with the author. When news broke about Shum's "Shadowhunters" casting, Clare shared on Tumblr that she had actually fan-cast him as Magnus years ago — "You probably know him from 'Glee,' ... but he's our Magnus now and his audition rocked it. Also, weirdly, I posted about him being Magnus three years ago." The author admitted that it was "pretty cool" for her dream casting to become a reality.

entertainment.title: Paul Howard, Son of Moe Howard of The Three Stooges, Dies at 91
entertainment.summary: He connected with fans of the iconic comedy act at conventions and hosted a nine-part 2015 docuseries called ‘Hey Moe, Hey Dad!’
entertainment.body:
Paul Howard, the only son of Moe Howard of The Three Stooges and the narrator of a nine-part 2015 docuseries about the legendary American comedy team, has died. He was 91.

Howard lived on Upper East Side of Manhattan and died this week, a spokesperson for C3 Entertainment, the owner of The Three Stooges license and brand, announced. He was the last remaining son of the original comedy team that consisted of Moe, his brothers Curly and Shemp and Larry Fine.

Since Moe’s death in 1975 at age 77, Paul Howard served as a guardian of his father’s legacy, offering fans a unique, firsthand view of the man behind the iconic bowl-cut hairdo and timeless slapstick comedy. Related Stories Movies Helene Hahn Loyd, Former Disney and DreamWorks SKG Exec, Dies at 78 TV Kimmarie Johnson, 'Beverly Hills, 90210' Actress, Dies at 50

He connected with generations of the Stooges faithful at conventions and events over the decades, sharing stories, memories and insights into the lives of his dad, his Uncle Shemp and his Uncle Curly.

The docuseries Hey Moe, Hey Dad! features rare archival footage, personal family accounts and interviews with members of the Howard, Fine and DeRita families (Curly Joe DeRita was another member of the Stooges act) and fans including Whoopi Goldberg and Leonard Maltin. (The series is available on The Three Stooges+ YouTube channel .)

Paramount Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Star Trek" may have a fantastical premise, but the best episodes of this iconic TV franchise told grounded stories rooted in lived realities, and their ability to examine political doctrines with a level of social awareness made those stories all the more intriguing. While this balance of futuristic environments and human-centric conflicts was one of the franchise's defining characteristics, it also led to seven episodes being either withheld, censored, or excluded from broadcast due to their taboo themes.

"Star Trek: The Original Series" accounts for more than half of these episodes, with four in particular having caught some unwanted attention from the BBC. Whether it was for overt violence, disturbing imagery, distressing themes, or sexual innuendo, the original show and its successors ended up crossing into controversial territory. Fortunately, all these episodes were later broadcast, with the unedited versions becoming available for the fans who never saw them the first time around.

NBC Season 3, Episode 14 of the original series, titled "Whom Gods Destroy," saw Spock (Leonard Nimoy) and Kirk (William Shatner) visit a Federation facility for the mentally ill to deliver a cure for the inmates. They discover the facility has been overrun and taken over by those same inmates, however, who are led by the villainous Captain Garth (Steve Ihnat). After acquiring the ability to shapeshift, Garth aims to escape and take over the galaxy. He impersonates the governor of the facility and captures Spock and Kirk, torturing Kirk in an attempt to uncover the codes for the USS Enterprise.

The episode aired on January 3, 1969, but it wasn't until January 19, 1994, that the BBC broadcast it. The fact that the premise revolved around the mentally ill meant that the episode was already treading dangerous waters, but the torture of Kirk and the numerous forced acts levied against the protagonists sealed the deal. In a letter to a fan, the BBC explained that this episode was one of four not broadcast because "they all dealt most unpleasantly with the already unpleasant subjects of madness, torture, sadism, and disease" (via Den of Geek ). Furthermore, the attempted seduction of Kirk by the Orion Marta (Yvonne Craig) gave the episode a touch of provocativeness, which might also have contributed to the episode being withheld.

entertainment.title: Lasso Breaks Down 5 Essential Tracks From His New Album ‘Objetos Frágiles en Ambientes Hostiles’
entertainment.summary: "It’s a dedication to anyone who’s trying to achieve their dreams," the Venezuelan singer/songwriter tells Billboard Español .
entertainment.body:
In his new studio album, Objetos Frágiles en Ambientes Hostiles , Venezuelan singer/songwriter Lasso delves into themes such as love, heartbreak and the contradictions of human relationships through 11 tracks that showcase an artistic evolution within his pop sound.

Released on Friday (Nov. 6) by Lasso Party under exclusive license from Interscope Records, the set includes previously released singles like “p0rn0grafía,” “superpoder,” “Tu Lunar” and “¡¡¡FELIZ ANIVERSARIO!!!,” alongside new tracks such as “preguntas que me hago,” “Perdóname por esta canción” and “PESADILLAS.” It also features two notable collaborations: the focus track “Borracho Otra Vez” with Ana Mena, and “Ojalá Que No Te Quiera Nadie” with Nina.

Produced by Manuel Lara, the album is rich in nuances, with new textures and arrangements that expand Lasso’s sound, catchy lyrics and his sweet, raspy pop-rock voice. It also marks his first release after parting ways with Universal Music Mexico, the label behind previous projects of his like Eva (2023) and Malcriado (2025).

“I’ve been writing [ Objetos Frágiles en Ambientes Hostiles ] for two years,” the Latin Grammy-winning artist tells Billboard Español . “I wrote about 200 songs; I’d never written so much before. But this album also comes from a period where I couldn’t release music — I was leaving a record label, and there’s a cool-off period during which you can’t release anything — so all I did was write, write, write. There were moments when I was very sad, and others when I was very happy.”

Out of those 200 songs, he selected the 20 best and, with the help of friends and colleagues, finalized the ones that would make the tracklist. The oldest among the 11 is “PESADILLAS,” while the newest is “¡¡¡FELIZ ANIVERSARIO!!!.”

Regarding the album title, which means “Fragile Objects in Hostile Environments,” Lasso explains that “it’s a dedication to anyone who’s trying to achieve their dreams.”

“The fragile objects are the dreams, and the hostile environment is the world that receives them, telling you, ‘You can’t do it, you’re not good enough, there are already too many like you, or there are too few like you,’ depending on what you’re doing,” he elaborates. “And it’s about that daily struggle of saying, ‘What I’m doing is amazing, and I’m going to convince you, no matter how hard it is.’”

Below, Lasso breaks down five essential tracks from Objetos Frágiles en Ambientes Hostiles .

entertainment.title: The Other Midterms Flip: Broadcast Networks, Led by NBC, Dominated Election Night Coverage
entertainment.summary: Broadcasters accounted for 57 percent of primetime viewing on Tuesday.
entertainment.body:
In addition to changing the composition of Congress and a number of statehouses, the midterm elections brought another kind of disruption to the status quo: For the first time in 6 election cycles, more people watched the returns come in on network TV than on cable.

Per Nielsen ratings, 31.21 million people watched primetime election coverage on 13 broadcast and cable outlets Tuesday, significantly more than the 25.43 million viewers for the 2022 midterms. Of that audience, 57 percent (17.79 million) watched on broadcast outlets (NBC, ABC, CBS, Univision, Telemundo and PBS), and just 43 percent (13.42 million) on cable channels. That’s exactly the inverse of four years ago, when 57 percent of viewers went to cable for midterm coverage.

It’s been 14 years since broadcast networks drew a clear majority of election night viewers (there was a roughly 50-50 split in 2016). That was also the last election a broadcaster led all comers on — and in both 2012 and this year, NBC finished first.

The network had 6.74 million viewers in primetime Tuesday, more than doubling its 2022 average. ABC also improved considerably, growing by 57 percent from four years ago to 5.19 million viewers. CBS was off the pace some at 2.76 million, but it also improved by 8 percent from 2022. Univision (1.54 million), Telemundo (1.06 million) and PBS (about 500,000) made up the rest of the broadcast total.

CNN and MS NOW also improved their numbers from 2022, but Fox News tumbled by almost 3.5 million viewers (though it still narrowly led its cable counterparts). The big three broadcasters, however, collectively gained more viewers than Fox News lost, so the off night for Fox doesn’t fully explain the shift in balance from cable to broadcast.

So what does? For one, cable as a whole has also suffered across-the-board declines in the past four years. Homes with multi-channel providers (cable, satellite or digital services like YouTube TV or Hulu + Live TV) only represent 42.5 percent of TV homes now, down from 52.3 percent four years ago. That represents a loss of more than 10 million households.

Some of it might also be ideological: Fox News leans right, and a night when Republicans took bruising losses might have helped drive ratings down there. MS NOW’s gains could similarly be put down to a blue wave helping the left-leaning channel.

Tuesday’s viewer leaders, ABC and NBC, work to project big-tent inclusiveness, which seems to have paid off some. Marc Greenstein, executive vp creative production and field operations for NBC News , pointed to reporting initiatives on the NBC Nightly News and Meet the Press that try go beyond the “left-right food fight,” as he put it, and explore substantive issues and points of commonality.

It's unclear if "Crystal Lake" will be getting a second season, but, in any case, Vinson's next TV role might be his biggest; he's been tapped to play Atreus opposite Dave Bautista's Kratos in the Prime Video adaptation of the "God of War" games. entertainment.title: Fox Agrees to Keep Roku Open to Rivals in Justice Department Greenlight
entertainment.summary: The deal gives Fox control over a platform that's the gateway to content for millions of households.
entertainment.body:
Logo text The Justice Department’s clearance of Fox Corp.’s $22 billion acquisition of Roku is coming with concessions.

As part of its agreement with the competition regulators, Fox said it would remain open to rivals, according to the Justice Department. The company will continue carrying non-Fox movies and TV shows for at least three years, ensure competing services aren’t pushed down in search results or denied prominent placement on home screens and make audience data available to third parties. It also agreed to maintain safeguards preventing it from sharing sensitive information about rival content providers, including data on what users search for, watch and click until at least 2029.

Fox on Friday closed the deal , creating a new power player in media and streaming. The deal catapults the company into a major player, with two of the largest free streaming video platforms in Tubi and Roku and a premium streaming service in Fox One. And through Roku, it gains control of a behemoth distribution platform through which millions of households access TV, including applications operated by competitors like Netflix, YouTube and Disney+.

In its investigation, the Justice Department concluded that the deal is “not likely to result in harm to competition” in free, ad-supported streaming.

“Additionally, the investigation found that, because Roku relies on a broad offering of content from many providers to attract consumers, the merged firm would suffer monetary and reputational harm if it attempted to use the Roku platform to harm FOX’s content rivals,” the Justice Department said.

The transaction gives Fox major sway over how audiences discover and access content. Roku’s operating system powers its own streaming devices and is built into TVs. Its home screen is the gateway to those services for a significant chunk of the United States: Viewers use it to find apps, search for programming and, perhaps most important, decide what to watch.

The megamerger has been more than a year in the making, though the deal closed in just five months.

The singer, born Faouzia Ouihya, debuted on the Billboard Canadian Hot 100 two months ago with “Unethical,” a single that dropped over a year ago and has gone viral in a big way.

The song has reached 150 million global streams and become her second most-streamed single. It continues to climb the charts, with a new peak in each of its eight weeks on the chart. Her virtuosic vocal delivery and emotion have turned it into a viral TikTok clip, with “Unethical” live performance clips circling across social media. Some fans have even tried their hand at singing the song. The official “Unethical” sound plays in over 44,000 Instagram Reels and over 533,000 TikTok posts .

Following its release, it received much acclaim, with Faouzia now sitting at over 10 million monthly listeners on Spotify. It’s been a slow and steady ascent for Faouzia that is now paying off. Faouzia has worked with some of the biggest acts across multiple genres, including David Guetta, Galantis, John Legend and Martin Solveig. She is even credited as a co-writer on Ye and Ty Dolla $ign’s “Beg Forgiveness,” released in 2024.

entertainment.title: Knicks React After Player Tyler Kolek Calls Taylor Swift Fakest Fan
entertainment.summary: The New York Knicks are pledging allegiance to Taylor Swift. Shortly after the NBA team’s point guard Tyler Kolek declared the Grammy winner as one of their fakest fans, the Knicks went on the...
entertainment.body:
The New York Knicks are pledging allegiance to Taylor Swift .

Shortly after the NBA team’s point guard Tyler Kolek declared the Grammy winner as one of their fakest fans, the Knicks went on the defensive for the “Love Story” singer.

“Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden,” a spokesperson for the team said in a Nov. 6 statement to E! News, “and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization.”

Kolek and his fellow point guard Miles James “Deuce” McBride found themselves in some trouble during an interview with NBA 2K League , when they were faced with the question: “Who’s the fakest celebrity fan you’ve seen sitting courtside in an NBA game?” And Kolek did his part to keep it 100 on the land, the sea, the sky—by calling out his perceived fair-weather fans.

“At the Knicks games, I would say it’s very performative,” Kolek mused in a video posted to YouTube Nov. 5, “like they just want to be seen at the game, they’re not necessarily fans.”

The 25-year-old , who is beginning his third season with the team, suggested that Swift wasn’t actually a big fan of the Knicks, noting that beyond seeing her at some playoff games, “I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.”

And while McBride , 26, agreed with his teammate, he was a little nervous about the admission, saying, “Swifties not gonna like that answer.”

Doubling down with his qualms about her fandom aside, Kolek did concede that the “Fortnight” singer—who married Travis Kelce at the Knicks home court of Madison Square Garden July 3— does have quite a packed schedule. As he put it, “I guess she’s got a lot going on so she can’t come all the time, but it’s a little performative.”

The 7th Heaven alum confessed that he was at risk of losing both his job and his home due to circumstances out of his control.

"My boss is going through some kind of mental crisis and I may be losing my job and home," London wrote in a message shared to X Nov. 5, before adding, "This can’t be happening again."

The 53-year-old—who played the younger minister to Reverend Eric Camden in the family drama as well as Griffin Holbrook in Party Of Five —elaborated that aside from acting in projects like this year's Amityville: Descendants of Darkness and 2025's Bone Face , he also enjoys traditional work.

"If anyone has a job and home for me out there, please let me know. I love working a real job on top of acting," the Mallrats star petitioned his followers, emphasizing that he was "a good person."

And the stressful circumstances have left London—dad to Lyrik , 19, with ex Melissa Cunningham and Wyatt , 12, with wife Juliet Reeves —questioning his future.

As the Tell Me You Love Me star wrote, "Why does this keep happening to me??"

London has faced difficult chapters before. He spoke about how addiction impacted his career and marriage to Cunningham on Celebrity Rehab in 2010. He was also arrested in 2004 and 2018 for incidents related to domestic violence , with London sharing in the 2025 documentary Hollywood Demons that the 2004 incident led to his firing from 7th Heaven , though he denied the allegations of abuse, according to People .

While responding to concern from his followers about his current job and housing predicament, the Babysitter star elaborated on why the developments were so disconcerting. As he put it, "I’ve been the happiest in years. This is gonna give me a stroke. I’m so confused and worried."

entertainment.title: Teddy Swims’ ‘Mr. Know It All’ Hits No. 1 on Billboard Pop Airplay Chart
entertainment.summary: The singer-songwriter scores his second leader at the format, after “Lose Control” in 2024.
entertainment.body:
Teddy Swims earns his second No. 1 on Billboard ’s Pop Airplay chart as “Mr. Know It All” ascends two spots to the top of the Nov. 14-dated ranking.

Released on SWIMS Int./Warner Records, the song becomes the singer-songwriter’s second leader at the format, after “Lose Control” reigned for two weeks in April 2024.

The Pop Airplay chart measures songs’ weekly plays, as tabulated by Mediabase and provided to Billboard by Luminate, on nearly 150 U.S. mainstream top 40 radio stations.

Swims has also hit the Pop Airplay top 10 with “Bad Dreams,” which reached No. 8 in April 2025, and “The Door” (No. 9, November 2024).

On the all-genre, multimetric Billboard Hot 100 , “Mr. Know It All,” which Swims cowrote, has hit a No. 26 high, likewise becoming Swims’ fourth top 40 hit, after “Bad Dreams” (No. 30), “The Door” (No. 24) and “Lose Control” (No. 1 for one week). “Lose Control” went on to rule as the No. 1 song on the 2024 year-end Hot 100 .

“I feel like every time I meet one, I’m grateful, but I’m never satisfied,” Swims told Billboard News ’ Tetris Kelly earlier this year of how he assesses goals. “The human eye sees, like, 20 miles ahead, right? So soon as you get that 20 miles, you’re seeing 20 more miles and you’re, like, there’s still much further to go. So I always try to celebrate the wins, but I want to be the best. I try to just be where my feet are and know that this is where I’m supposed to be.”

Added the father of a now-16-month-old, “I just also want my son to think I’m cool.”

All charts dated Nov. 14 will update Tuesday, Nov. 10, on Billboard.com.

"Marshals" marked Green's first professional acting role. He's better known as a country music star.

Green is the voice behind top Billboard hits such as "Worst Way" and "Change My Mind." His collaborations with other high-profile artists like Ella Langley, Luke Combs, and Thomas Rhett have also done well on the charts. Even if you're not a country music aficionado, you may recognize Green from his most unconventional partnership yet: "Alabama Vs. Tennessee," a duet with former quarterback Peyton Manning about a major college football rivalry.

Green has appeared in front of the camera before, but only in connection with his music career. He's filmed several music videos and debuted as a coach on Season 30 of "The Voice." Despite his lack of prior acting credits, Green's "Marshals" performance has garnered praise from audiences. "This was real acting, and I'm so glad," he told TVLine in April 2026. "I didn't want to tiptoe into this world where I show up as a country singer and play a song. I wanted it to be a real role, and man, what an awesome place to start in the acting world on a show like this."

Fred Hayes/CBS Although Riley Green wanted his "Marshals" role to be more than a musical cameo, his music career still came in handy. In Episode 9, the singer played one of his own songs, "My Way," for Kayce Dutton (Luke Grimes) and the rest of the team around a campfire.

Green's experience onstage also helped him convey Garrett's emotions on camera. "When you write a song, you're coming up with these thoughts for the first time so those emotions are real ... But when you go and you perform that song over and over and over again, you have to keep it feeling real, even when maybe it's not so much," he explained in an interview with People . "So for me, if I'm playing a song that's a really emotional song, there is a feeling that I need to get to go and perform it that way. And acting's very similar in that sense."

Green hasn't announced any additional acting projects as of this writing, but he's still interested in taking on more roles. "I'd really like to be able to go to one place and kind of settle in," he said in the same interview. "I think it'd be helpful to stay in that world for a little."

entertainment.title: David Del Valle, Admired Historian of Horror Films, Dies at 77
entertainment.summary: He provided commentary for many home video releases and conducted what many consider to be the quintessential Vincent Price interview.
entertainment.body:
David Del Valle, the encyclopedic horror film historian, author and raconteur who contributed to dozens of laserdisc, DVD and Blu-ray commentary tracks during his eclectic career, has died. He was 77.

Del Valle died Wednesday at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank after a battle with esophageal cancer, his caregiver and friend, producer Dano Marino, told The Hollywood Reporter .

He was living down the street from the apartment on Harold Way in Los Angeles where Dracula star Bela Lugosi died of a heart attack in 1956. “The only way out of Harold Way is apparently feet first,” he joked. Related Stories Movies Sebastián Lelio, Chilean Filmmaker Behind 'Disobedience,' 'The Wonder' and the Oscar-Winning 'A Fantastic Woman,' Dies at 52 Movies Helene Hahn Loyd, Former Disney and DreamWorks Exec, Dies at 78

Del Valle produced and hosted a series of cable TV interviews under the Sinister Image umbrella in which he spoke with the likes of Vincent Price, Cameron Mitchell, Russ Meyer and Curtis Harrington. His hourlong chat with Price in 1987 is considered the most substantial interview the horror legend ever gave.

He also wrote the books Lost Horizons Beneath the Hollywood Sign and Six Reels Under , published in 2010 and 2012, respectively, and articles for Fangoria magazine; penned an online column called “Camp David” for Films in Review ; and introduced a weekly screening of horror films in 2020 for the channel/app Full Moon Features.

Del Valle’s 120 or so movie commentaries included those for such companies as the Criterion Collection ( Count Yorga ), Severin Films ( Horrors of Spider Island , Bloody Pit of Horror , An Angel for Satan , Nightmare Castle ), Kino Lorber ( The Amazing Transparent Man, The Man Who Reclaimed His Head ), Synapse Films ( Suspiria ), Scream Factory ( The Fly ) and Arrow Films.

Del Valle knew personally most of the people he wrote and talked about and was known for his wicked sense of humor and skills as a storyteller. “He never wanted to grow up in all the most charming ways,” Marino said.

An only child, Ronald David Del Valle was born on Sept. 24, 1949, in El Paso, Texas. He said his love of horror began with the classic Universal monster movies of the 1930s.

entertainment.title: How long Thomas Markle Sr. could serve in prison revealed after child pornography arrest

entertainment.body:
Thomas Markle Sr. could be calling prison home for the rest of his life after his arrest for possession of child pornography .

Shari Karney, a national legal analyst and attorney, exclusively told Page Six, “Federal child pornography possession sentences can be substantial. Recent federal sentencing statistics put the average possession sentence at approximately 83 months — nearly seven years behind bars.”

The attorney and survivor’s rights advocate continued, “Twenty years behind bars could effectively mean Thomas Markle dies in federal custody. At 82, even a five- or ten-year sentence could amount to a life sentence.”

According to a press release from the Department of Justice, Markle “would face a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison.”

In the criminal complaint obtained by Page Six, Markle appeared in two of the images alongside an underage girl. The filing claims a witness identified him as the adult in the photographs.

Karney said this alleged evidence could “raise questions investigators must pursue.”

Markle could use his dementia diagnosis to help shorten his sentence, as the attorney explained, “His age, dementia, amputation, and other serious medical problems could significantly affect sentencing. A defense attorney will undoubtedly argue that a lengthy prison term would be tantamount to a death sentence.

“Being elderly, disabled, or the father of a duchess does not confer immunity from criminal prosecution. The law does not have a royal-family exception.”

entertainment.title: Incubus Frontman Brandon Boyd Making Feature Scoring Debut With Sci-Fi Thriller ‘Unknown Company’ (Exclusive)

entertainment.body:
Logo text Brandon Boyd, the frontman of rock band Incubus , is making his debut as a feature scoring composer.

The vocalist and songwriter has teamed up with indie musician and composer Gregory Rogove to score Unknown Company , an indie World War II sci-fi thriller starring The Walking Dead actor Ross Marquand that is now in post-production.

Directed by Vincent Talenti ( Transformers: War for Cybertron ) and written by Gavin Hignight ( Gundam: Requiem for Vengeance), Unknown Company follows a small unit of American soldiers dispatched behind enemy lines in the final days of World War II to recover the wreckage of an unidentified object. What begins as a military mission becomes a confrontation with something beyond their understanding, testing the soldiers’ loyalty to one another and their sense of what is real. Talenti is producing the feature alongside Eva Ceja, Dylan Palley and Matt Ryan. Bret Rudnick serves as executive producer.

I’m a huge horror and sci-fi fan and I immediately felt intuitions about the sounds and moods that needed to accompany this picture. The film is creepy, beautiful and dark and we composed music that meets the film there.”

entertainment.summary: Katy Perry’s history with Russell Brand was not included in his rape trial. After the disgraced comedian was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in London’s...
entertainment.body:
Katy Perry ’s history with Russell Brand was not included in his rape trial.

After the disgraced comedian was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in London’s Southwark Crown Court, the prosecution confirmed why Brand’s 14-month marriage to Perry in 2010 was not part of their opening arguments.

“The prosecution recognize that matters post 2009 involving his relationship with Katy Perry may be sensitive,” lead prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC said in a pre-trial submissions statement, per The Telegraph , “as may his previous faiths, and we are content to remove these from the opening.”

Similarly, the “Teenage Dream” singer—now mom to a 6-year-old daughter with ex Orlando Bloom —was not asked to provide any kind of witness statement during the police investigation into Brand.

While Perry was not involved in the investigation or trial—which included allegations of events that occurred between 2004 and 2009, the same year Brand and Perry started dating—in any way, Brand briefly mentioned his relationship to the Grammy nominee while testifying during the trail, sharing how he achieved “staggering fame” at that time in his life.

Following the guilty verdict, the Forgetting Sarah Marshall alum—who was cleared of two separate counts of rape as well as one count of indecent assault—was told by presiding judge Joel Bennathan that he plans to sentence the actor to “significant custodial time,” while also denying him bail. Brand’s sentencing is set to take place on Monday, Nov. 9.

E! News reached out to Brand’s attorneys for comment, as well as his and Perry’s representatives, but has not yet heard back.

In the years since his marriage to Perry, Brand—father to three kids with wife Laura Brand —has reemerged in the public eye as a right-winged Christian influencer. And he has acknowledged his faith while denying the allegations against him.
