entertainment.summary: Exquisite news: The deal starts off with Blumhouse boarding the adaptation of hit comic 'Exquisite Corpses.'
entertainment.body:
Logo text Comic book creator James Tynion IV and his production banner Tiny Onion has signed a first-look deal with Blumhouse Atomic , the horror powerhouse run by Jason Blum and James Wan.

The deal begins with a bang as Blumhouse joins Tiny Onion and Lyrical Media in working on an adaptation of Exquisite Corpses , Tynion’s best-selling and award-winning comic book universe centered on a serial killer battle royale. The title, which Tynion created with artist Michael Walsh, is being developed across both film and animation.

Blumhouse Atomic and Tiny Onion are already working on a movie adaptation of Tynion’s horror comic Something Is Killing the Children , with Craig Zobel recently boarding as director. The good vibes led to the first-look and partnership on Corpses . Related Stories Business Jason Blum and James Wan Rename Their Company News 'Beneath the Trees Where Nobody Sees' Final Act Gets Title and Cover (Exclusive)

“James has been a valued partner on Something Is Killing The Children , which is why we wanted to expand our relationship. He has great storytelling instincts with a passion for the horror genre,” said Blum, CEO and co-founder of Blumhouse Atomic. “As we look to develop more IP, this felt like a great fit, and we’re happy to take the next step with him and Tiny Onion.”

Stated Tynion, “From the moment I first stepped into the Blumhouse offices, it felt like coming home. Every person in that building, and every filmmaker on their roster is dedicated to making great horror, and I’m thrilled to stand by their side and help bring these terrifying stories to life.”

Corpses has a killer premise: Every five years on Halloween, the 13 oldest and richest families in America play a game of control in which their so-called champions, recruited killers of various stripes, descend upon an unsuspecting town and fight until the last slayer standing determines the winner. The initial 13-issue series, which wrapped earlier this year, told of the various townspeople trying to survive the night as killers with monickers such as Lone Gunman, Fox Mask Killer, Pretty Boy, Rascal Randy, and Lady Carolina ran through their town.

Corpses has sold over one million copies in its first eighteen months of publication by Image Comics. There are now three spin-off series focusing on some of the killers and a second overarching mini-series, with new killers, is planned for next year.

entertainment.summary: If you're craving more shows like 9-1-1, look no further. These five first responder shows feature the same over-the-top disasters and found family dynamics.
entertainment.body:
Disney/Christopher Willard Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover " 9-1-1" is one of the most outrageously fun shows on TV right now, and though it's one of many first responder shows currently airing, nothing beats "9-1-1" when it comes to over-the-top disasters and big emotions. Indeed, we love the show's entertainingly unrealistic emergencies just as much as we love its focus on the wholesome found family of Station 118.

The audacious procedural — created by Ryan Murphy, Tim Minear, and Brad Falchuk — is in the midst of its 10th season, with no signs of slowing down (though the city of Los Angeles might be tired of a new doomsday-esque catastrophe every year). If those 100+ episodes of firefighting drama — and two spinoffs — aren't enough for you, we've got you thrill-seekers covered. Here's a handful of shows that will remind you of "9-1-1" while bringing a new set of emergencies to the table. If you love experiencing an adrenaline rush (and the occasional tear-fest) from the comfort of your couch, these series are for you.

NBC Though Dick Wolf didn't create "Chicago Fire" with franchise aspirations , it has since evolved into a Chicago-based universe looking at different groups of first responders (and a few lawyers). Still, "Chicago Fire" remains the best "One Chicago" TV show , and it's one of the most solid firefighter shows we've seen. As in "9-1-1," the firefighters and paramedics at Firehouse 51 in "Chicago Fire" are like a family, and their bond is the show's emotional anchor.

Plot-wise, the series centers the emergencies above all else (though later seasons have become a bit more melodramatic when it comes to interpersonal issues), and focuses on the gritty, dangerous work of firefighting. Despite the peril the protagonists find themselves in on a daily basis — and indeed, no one is safe from grievous injury or death on this show — "Chicago Fire" transmits a message of hope and resilience, balancing the heartbreak with plenty of heartwarming moments.

Lindsay Sarazin/Paramount+ If you like the silliness of "9-1-1" and the general sense of optimism it portrays, you may really dig "SkyMed," a Canadian series about a group of young, attractive nurses and pilots saving lives in rural Manitoba. These strapping heroes are a diverse crew, featuring Indigenous actors, LGBTQ characters, and a focus on mental health issues.

Though "SkyMed" adheres to the classic tropes of the first responder drama in many ways, the air ambulance concept and the gorgeous landscapes give it some added appeal. Plus, an interest in issues facing First Nations communities gives the show a unique perspective not often found in procedurals like this.

entertainment.title: Hear Fiona Apple and the Bolt Cutters Cover Mother Earth’s ‘Revolution’
entertainment.summary: Song was culled for Right Now album benefitting Doctors Without Borders
entertainment.body:
Fiona Apple and the Bolt Cutters have covered Mother Earth’s “Revolution.” The song is set to appear on the Dougie Bowne-produced Right Now , which will benefit Doctors Without Borders.

Their rendition of the 1968 protest song was shared on the Instagram of Zelda Hallman, Apple’s roommate and best friend. The song was produced by the Bolt Cutters — Apple, Davíd Garza, Sebastian Steinberg, and Amy Aileen Wood, with each of their parts recorded remotely from locales including Los Angeles, Houston, and from the East Coast. “Amy masterfully brought them together to capture this moment’s energy,” they said in a statement.

The powerful song is an apt choice to cover now following this week’s midterm elections results , a blue tsunami happily celebrated by many music fans. “There’s a new world a comin’ near/Singing loud and clear/Revolution,” Apple soulfully sings. “Feel that rumblin’ along the ground; It’s a mighty sound/Revolution.”

In the statement accompanying the post, which features a photo of the group as the song plays, Hallman shared in the caption, “America is changing. You can feel it. It has a pulse, and it’s growing. This week’s election gave us something we’ve needed: hope for a more progressive, compassionate, inclusive, and just future. Tuesday was a victory, but only a beginning.” The post continued: “Because something is happening. All across the world, people are marching for justice, freedom, and peace. Dockworkers are refusing to lend their labor to weapons shipments. People are confronting ICE, demanding freedom for Palestine, and calling for an end to the bombing of Gaza. From Ukraine to Sudan, the Congo, Yemen, and Myanmar, civilians face war, hunger, and displacement. “People are fighting for reproductive rights, bodily autonomy, health care, and equal protection — regardless of race, religion, gender, or immigration status. For due process instead of detention and deportation without a fair hearing,” the statement reads. “For treaties with Indigenous peoples and Tribal Nations to be honored, and for justice for Native, Black, and LGBTQ+ communities. Especially for those deaths and disappearances of young people that remain unsolved and poorly explained.”

entertainment.title: JonBenét Ramsey's Brother Burke Shares "Best Chance" at Solving Murder
entertainment.summary: JonBenét Ramsey's brother has not given up on the search for her killer nearly three decades later. Breaking his 10-year public silence, Burke Ramsey detailed his belief that DNA belonging to an...
entertainment.body:
JonBenét Ramsey 's brother has not given up on the search for her killer nearly three decades later.

Breaking his 10-year public silence, Burke Ramsey detailed his belief that DNA belonging to an "unknown male intruder" found on his slain sister's underwear and beneath her finger may be "the best evidence we have."

"We need to find that match," he told the Daily Mail in an interview published Nov. 5. "It's probably the person who did it, you know, and it's the best chance we have to solve this."

"And I want it solved," the 39-year-old continued. "I don't know much about the scientific nitty-gritty and it's hard to learn the details of the case, because it is emotionally taxing. But they need to send those samples to different labs again and keep testing."

He added, "Find the match. That will go a long way to bringing justice."

Burke was 9 years old when his sister JonBenét, 6, was reported missing from their family’s Colorado home on Dec. 26, 1996. Her body was eventually found in the basement, with her cause of death ruled as asphyxia by strangulation and blunt head trauma.

In 2003, Burke and his parents, John Bennett Ramsey and the late Patsy Ramsey , were ruled out as contributors to the unknown DNA discovered on JonBenét. And though Burke in particular has been the subject of many online theories, he and the Ramsay family has long denied his involvement in his sister’s death .

Aside from DNA evidence, which John alleged in 2024 hadn’t been tested , investigators through the years have also homed in on a handwritten ransom note for $118,000 found in the Ramseys' family home on the day of JonBenét disappearance.

entertainment.body:
As it turns out, everybody wants more Kristen Bell and Adam Brody .

Following the success of season three of Nobody Wants This , Netflix confirmed the romantic comedy was renewed for a fourth season.

The exciting news was also confirmed by Bell, who shared on Instagram Nov. 6 that “season 4 is coming” alongside a clip from season three—in which Brody’s character proposes—of her and fellow costars Justine Lupe and Timothy Simons excitedly celebrating.

The show’s creator Erin Foster was also overjoyed by the news, resharing the video to her Instagram Story with the caption, “It’s official.”

She and her fellow producers Jenni Konner and Bruce Eric Kaplan shared their excitement in a Nov. 6 press release from Netflix, joking, “We are so happy and thrilled to do another season of our favorite show on television, which coincidentally is the one we run.”

And the show is extra special for Foster as she was inspired to create Nobody Wants This based on her own experiences with husband Simon Tikhman . In fact, season three’s proposal episode was actually inspired by how Tikhman proposed to her in 2019, fake wedding and all.

“About a month before he proposed,” Foster narrated an Oct. 28 Instagram video , “we got this invitation to a wedding vow renewal. It had attire and a schedule for the whole weekend.”

And while Foster flew to Napa Valley fully expecting to attend a wedding, she was instead surprised by a proposal, as well as both her and Tikhman’s families jumping out to celebrate after hiding in a barn during the proposal.

Cipriani Wall Street was buzzing Thursday night as Australia’s most influential trans-Pacific power players, media heavyweights and diplomatic glitterati descended for the 2026 American Australian Association Benefit Dinner to honor News Corp’s chief executive, Robert Thomson.

Hosted by former South Australian premier and Association president Steven Marshall, the annual black-tie affair boasted quite the guest list, including Rupert Murdoch and his son Lachlan, former Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott, US Ambassador to Australia under Barack Obama Jeffrey Bleich, now an international special envoy at AI powerhouse Anthropic, and Australia’s diplomatic heavyweights Greg Moriarty and James Larsen.

The Murdochs, whose family connection to the Association dates back to its founding in 1948 by Rupert’s father, Sir Keith Murdoch, were among the evening’s most anticipated arrivals.

But the night belonged to Thomson, News Corp’s CEO who received the Lifetime Achievement Award.

Introduced by Lachlan Murdoch, the veteran journalist and former editor of The Times and managing editor of The Wall Street Journal was recognized for his extraordinary career and contribution to the Australia–US relationship.

And then came a rather special musical moment: Australian singer-songwriter Nick Cave took to the stage to perform.

The evening also featured remarks from Consul-General Heather Ridout AO, St Vincent’s Health Australia’s Dr Christopher Robinson and Association Scholar Yasmin Zaman, whose pioneering work in space medicine showcased the next generation of Australian talent.

Ambassador Greg Moriarty reflected on the alliance ahead of the 75th anniversary of ANZUS, while Sarah Lipe and her band sent guests home with a spirited set of Australian classics.

sports.title: NFC North has 17-3 record against non-NFC North teams
sports.summary: The NFC North is the best division in the NFL.
sports.body:
The Vikings, Bears, Lions, and Packers have a combined record of 17-3 against non-NFC North teams. Via NBC Sports research, the ensuing 85 percent success rate is the highest by any division in the NFL since the 1970 merger.

In theory, all four teams of the NFC North could make the playoffs. To do that, however, each would have to finish higher in the wild-card pecking order than the Rams and the Seahawks (assuming the 49ers win the NFC West).

This week, two teams of the NFC North have an easier path to victory than the others; the Bears host the Buccaneers and the Lions visit the Dolphins.

For the Packers (who play the Patriots in New England) and the Vikings (who play the Bills on Monday night), it will be harder to keep pushing 17-3 to 21-3.

sports.title: In defending his willingness to spend, Jerry Jones may have admitted to tampering
sports.summary: On Friday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tried to reverse the perception/reality that he deliberately underspends on coaches.
sports.body:
“I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on,” Jones said on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas.

Unless he was referring to college coaches (or high-school coaches), that’s tampering. Period. End of discussion.

It could be false — an effort to bolster the idea that, yes, he’s willing to spend. Still, the effort to put out the frugality fire he started on Tuesday by ridiculously claiming there’s no correlation between coaching pay and winning included a nonchalant concession that he has tried to pry NFL coaches away from their current teams, in blatant violation of the rules.

Will the NFL look into this one? Probably not. Because the league office surely realizes, as the rest of us do, that Jerry was simply saying whatever he had to say to lessen the impact of the accidental truth he told on Tuesday regarding a deliberate reluctance to do whatever he needs to do to make his team as good as it can be.

sports.title: Brandon Aiyuk: I’m back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated
sports.summary: The wide receiver and his agent are meeting with the 49ers about Aiyuk's future.
sports.body:
The wide receiver arrived at the team’s business offices in a van with his agent Friday afternoon to meet with the 49ers and presumably negotiate a resolution.

“Obviously, Brandon is here to meet with the team,” Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk’s agent, said before the meeting, via video from David Lombardi of the San Francisco Standard. “Fortunately, he’s feeling good physically. He’s healthy . He’s ready to get back to work. Don’t really have any comment about where he’s going to play. We’ll keep that between us and the Niners. But obviously we’re here with all the right intentions.”

Aiyuk last played in a game on Oct. 20, 2024, when he tore the ACL and MCL in his right knee. The relationship between the team and the player fell apart after that, and the 49ers voided the guaranteed money due to his unwillingness to rehab at their facility.

The 49ers placed him on the reserve/left squad list on Dec. 13, 2025. Rosenhaus filed a reinstatement request on Oct. 27, but the NFL still hasn’t reinstated him.

“Nice to see you all,” Aiyuk said. “I’m feeling great, feeling healthy. It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process. But I’m back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League.”

49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said earlier in the day he "[couldn’t] care less” how the meeting went since “ it’s been over for our football team for a long time.”

sports.title: Brandon Aiyuk plans to meet with 49ers at team's business offices, not team facility
sports.summary: 49ers tight end George Kittle was right, sort of.
sports.body:
Per agent Drew Rosenhaus, Friday’s meeting will happen at the team’s business offices and not at the team’s practice facility.

That makes the session not a formal reporting-for-duty by Aiyuk, in the hopes of forcing the team’s hand. As explained earlier today, the NFL still hasn’t reinstated Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list — even though Rosenhaus filed the request on October 27.

Instead, it’s a meeting presumably aimed at negotiating a resolution to the situation.

The 49ers pushed to reporters on Thursday night the idea that Aiyuk’s return to the NFL is tied to the $13 million the team believes he owes in previously paid signing bonus. That shouldn’t be part of the analysis as to whether he’s reinstated by the league, whether the 49ers put him on the roster again, and/or whether the 49ers cut him.

But they’re making it an issue, because they can tie his ability to play to his willingness to wire the disputed funds to the team.

So that’s what’s happening. The brakes already have been applied to what should have been an administrative and automatic process. The league and the 49ers are working together to help the team get money back from Aiyuk before Aiyuk is permitted to get back into the league.

Then there’s the fact that an active arrest warrant is pending for Aiyuk, arising from a speeding incident. The business meeting could potentially be interrupted by an attempt to enforce a specific item of police business.

sports.title: Nick Sirianni admits that he misled reporters about quarterback situation
sports.summary: Instead of covering up one lie with another lie, Sirianni opted to tell the truth that he hadn't.
sports.body:
Because they all do. Particularly in so-called “must-lie” situations.

There’s an art to it. A way to conceal a lie with another lie. On Friday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted not to lie about the fact that he lied on Monday when he told reporters that quarterback Tanner McKee would not be benched.

“ Tanner’s our guy ,” Sirianni said. “We’re not making any changes there.”

On Wednesday, the Eagles made a change there, elevating Joe Milton over McKee. The move was announced after Sirianni had his midweek media availability, which prevented him from being asked questions about the change in position from “Tanner’s our guy” to “Tanner’s not our guy.”

On Friday, Sirianni finally faced the music regarding his comments from Monday. In lieu of coming up with an explanation premised on the idea that what he said was true when he said it and circumstances changed, Sirianni surprisingly admitted that he wasn’t telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth to reporters and, in turn, the fans.

“I was going to hold onto that as long as I possibly could, every second, every minute,” Sirianni said. “Again, I’m not real shy with you guys. I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y’all have to do, but I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I’m always going to protect the team first and foremost.

“Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there’s a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside.”

In an industry where the truth is only told when it’s coincidental to strategic interests, it’s jarring that Sirianni told the truth that he was lying. It would have been easy to say, “We took a more careful look at the situation after Monday.” Or, even more simply, “We changed our mind. Shit happens.”

sports.title: Ben Johnson: Jeffery Simmons has had a dramatic impact on the Bears

“I think it’s been fairly dramatic. I think you saw it in the game last week. There’s no doubt about it,” Johnson said of Simmons’ impact.

Johnson continued by discussing the importance of players who play great on the field during games but also exude greatness in everything they do during the week.

“We keep preaching to our guys the consistency of how we go about our business, what we do in the building, and what we do on game day. That’s what good teams do. Really, that’s what great teams do, is bring that same juice an energy throughout the week and into the game as well,” Johnson said.

sports.title: Antonio Brown pleads guilty to aggravated assault with a firearm
sports.summary: Former NFL receiver Antonio Brown, who was charged with attempted murder after a May 2025 shooting in Miami, has pleaded guilty to a lesser charge.
sports.body:
Via ESPN, Brown pleaded guilty to aggravated assault with a firearm on Friday. He was sentenced to three years probation.

Conditions include attending weekly counseling sessions and not possessing a firearm.

If all terms are met, the probation could end in roughly 18 months. Also, the guilty plea to a felony charge would not be on his official record.

“Antonio and I are extremely grateful that this matter has finally been resolved. He faced a thirty-year prison sentence, including a twenty-year mandatory minimum,” Brown’s attorney, Mark Eiglarsh, said in a statement issued to ESPN. “The prosecutors offered to reduce the charge and allow him to serve probation without a conviction. Given the stakes, it was an offer we couldn’t refuse.”

The case would have hinged on the application of Florida’s “stand your ground” law, given that Brown claimed he fired a weapon at another man in self-defense. The facts would have made it difficult for Brown to show that he believed he was facing death or serious injury; he allegedly grabbed a gun from a security guard and fired at a man after an alleged assault on Brown had ended and the target of the bullets had disengaged from Brown.

Brown spent 12 years in the NFL, playing for the Steelers, Raiders (although he never appeared in a regular-season game), the Patriots, and the Buccaneers.

sports.title: Jerry Jones scrambles to rectify his comments about coaching pay
sports.summary: The gaslighting of Cowboys fans continues.
sports.body:
On Tuesday, Jones made a nonsensical case for the notion that there’s “zero correlation” between coaching pay and wins. On Friday, Jones argued that he’s willing to pay for coaches — notwithstanding his unmistakable claim that there’s no connection between paying big money to coaches and getting big results.

“ No one will ever know if I’ve ever been interested in somebody that at the time was known to have, let’s say, a substantive financial marketplace,” Jones said in his latest appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. “No one will ever know. Well, the facts are I have been out there, and I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on. And knew full well that I was going to pay them for all their success. . . . It is absolutely ridiculous, and I actually grin when somebody says, ‘Jerry’s not willing to pay the money to get the right kind of coach out there. . . .’ I have five wells that cost more than any coach I know of, each one of them, in the NFL.”

He can grin all he wants. But he said what he said. And now he’s saying something different because the reaction was universal.

There’s absolutely a connection between paying for a good coach and reaping the rewards of having one.

Pointing to his oil wells is gaslighting. Jones personally doesn’t see the benefit in paying a lot of money for an accomplished coach. So he’d rather treat the pursuit of a good coach like prospecting, searching for a low-rent coach who generates penthouse results.

The other factor is the power that flows from signing a coach to a market-level deal. Enough power to ignore Jones and to coach the team as he sees fit, confident that Jerry won’t fire him and risk owing the full buyout.

So why did Jerry react the way he did? He needs the fans to think he’s “all in” when it comes to chasing a championship (or, at a minimum, the franchise’s first berth in the NFC Championship in 31 years and counting). The moment fans realize that it’s all bluster and carnival barking and penny pinching is the moment they’ll stop going to Cowboys games and start looking for another team to support.

Tuesday’s comments were far too revealing. And, for loyal fans who give their time, money, and emotion to the Cowboys, far too damning regarding the manner in which the General Manager who can’t be fired is mismanaging the team.

sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings have been playing football against each other since 1971. But in more than five decades, they’ve met just 15 times. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings have been playing football against each other since 1971. But in more than five decades, they’ve met just 15 times. Minnesota holds a 9-6 advantage in the all-time series, although Buffalo has won four of the past six meetings. And, while there aren’t a whole lot of games to choose from, there are certainly a few worth remembering. There’s the afternoon Drew Bledsoe threw for more than 400 yards. The day a rookie Josh Allen introduced himself to the NFL by hurdling a linebacker. And, of course, there’s that game in 2022 that Bills fans would probably rather forget. So, before Allen heads back to Minnesota, we’re opening the Time Capsule to revisit five of the more memorable meetings between the Bills and Vikings, starting with a comeback in 1982. _____________________________________________________________________________ 1982 — A comeback worth remembering The Minnesota Vikings had a 19-0 lead over Buffalo on Sept. 16, 1982, and every reason to think they had the game under control. Joe Ferguson, however, had other plans. The Bills offense was a little late to the party, but it was about to make up for lost time. Ferguson threw for 330 yards and three touchdowns as Buffalo rallied for a 23-22 win. He got the Bills on the scoreboard with a 6-yard touchdown pass to Frank Lewis before halftime, then connected with Jerry Butler for a 4-yard score in the third quarter. Minnesota still held a 22-13 lead heading into the fourth, but a 21-yard field goal from Nick Mike-Mayer brought Buffalo within six. Ferguson and Butler connected again, this time from 11 yards out, and Mike-Mayer’s extra point gave the Bills the win. _____________________________________________________________________________ 2002 — An overtime shootout The Bills and Vikings combined for 78 points on Sept. 15, 2002, and somehow needed extra time and another six points to find a winner. Drew Bledsoe threw for a franchise-record 463 yards, but Buffalo needed a little last-second magic just to get the game into overtime. The Bills had taken a 36-32 lead on Bledsoe’s 3-yard touchdown pass to Peerless Price with 3:08 remaining, only for Minnesota to answer with a touchdown of its own and go ahead 39-36 with 26 seconds left. Bledsoe got Buffalo into position for a Mike Hollis 54-yard field goal as regulation expired. Then Bledsoe and Price delivered the finish.

But at the snap is when the calculated chaos ensued. Cornerback Byron Murphy, who initially looked to be covering Christian Watson in a tight split near the numbers on the upper portion of the screen, screamed off the edge as a blitzer. Regarding the veteran reinforcements at that position, we’ll see if the Bills want to upgrade over Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone. Outside cornerback is also an option too despite the recently stable play from rookie Davison Igbinosun and Christian Benford returning to his super steady ways. Linebacker or even edge rusher aren’t out of the question either. Anticipation is building quickly, as the trade deadline is now only four days away.

Well… let’s just say the shine has worn off Baltimore’s season with quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both going on Injured Reserve. Yes, the Ravens
sports.body: Tonight’s game between the Baltimore Ravens and Jacksonville Jaguars once held a lot of promise as a truly great matchup in primetime. Now? Well… let’s just say the shine has worn off Baltimore’s season with quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both going on Injured Reserve. Yes, the Ravens lost two quarterbacks to significant injuries in their loss to the Buffalo Bills. Adding insult here, emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano also picked up an injury in relief. Despite that, Fagnano gets his first official NFL start tonight as Week 9 gets underway with Thursday Night Football. It’s a massive challenge for Fagnano, who must try to lead a nose-diving Ravens teams to a win against a Jacksonville Jaguars team that seems as well-rounded as any in the league. With time to prep as the team’s QB1, Fagnano should look a little more game ready. There’s scant professional film on him, but what there is shows a quarterback who couldn’t solve the Bills’ defense in Week 8. Baltimore’s coaching staff will keep their fingers crossed that things go well enough, otherwise the team will be forced to turn to quarterback Kevon Slovis. It feels like we’re set for a blowout this evening, but strange things do happen on Thursday nights. Do the Ravens roll out the smart play and run everything on offense through running back Derrick Henry? It’s not a terrible idea, but they don’t seem to have quite the offensive line and blocking Henry enjoyed in prior seasons. Would it be terrible if they better-incorporated Henry in the passing attack? You’d find no argument from me on the matter. This is a huge challenge for the Ravens against a 5-2 Jaguars team we’ve barely discussed. Jacksonville has an enormous lead in the AFC South, with the 2-5 Houston Texans in second among a mostly moribund division. One of few teams to defeat the Bills at home during the playoffs, there’s little love lost between Bills Mafia and those who cry “Duuuuval.” That’s right, Rumblers: Tonight you’re Ravens fans. Buffalo stands to benefit from a Jaguars loss, even though the Bills currently have the top spot in the AFC race to the playoffs. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 9 of Thursday Night Football. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.body: The New York Jets are 2-6. Plenty of people have written in permanent marker that the Jets will inevitably be 2-8 if we fast-forward two weeks. Up next is a road game against the Kansas City Chiefs and a home tilt versus the Buffalo Bills. Don’t tell that noise to Jets starting quarterback Geno Smith. “For me, again, it doesn’t matter what anyone else thinks. It’s about what we think and what we believe. If the Jets are going to upset the Chiefs, who are a 10-point favorite at home, they have to believe in themselves. The green and white have the pieces in place to pull off the upset.
